sources.citation: Harvey, Mark. 2001. A grammar of Limilngan: a language of the Mary River region, Northern Territory, Australia. Pacific Linguistics 516. Canberra.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Phonology is Limilngan's only. On Uwinymil (p. 10): 'This language is extinct; the last speaker Mr Stanley Baker having died in 1984. There are only very limited materials on this language (these are analysed in Harvey MSb.). These materials nevertheless suffice to establish that Uwinymil is distinct from Limilngan, and that it is a member of the Gunwinyguan language family.' Reference list: 'Harvey, Mark, MSb, Uwinymil.'

sources.citation: AIATSIS. AUSTLANG: N37.1 Uwinymil. Australian Indigenous Languages Database, Canberra (the Internet Archive snapshot of 16 Dec 2019; live page returns not reachable by automated download to automated clients).
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.source_kind: database or survey citing another work
sources.note: No phonology content. Documentation table: Word list None (0), Text collection None (0), Grammar None (0), Audio-visual None (0); 'Manuscript note: not available'; Grammar -; Dictionary -. Comment quotes Harvey: extinct, very similar to Warray N25, often confused with Limilngan N42 but unrelated (1986); distinct language per Harvey 2003:285. References: Baker Top End Handbook (ASEDA 0626); Harvey 1986 Kamu fieldnotes MS 2551; Harvey 2003; Harvey 2008 AILEC 0802; Sutton 1995; Tindale 1974; names from Harvey PMS 5822 and Basedow 1907.

sources.citation: Evans, Nicholas (ed.). 2003. The non-Pama-Nyungan languages of northern Australia: comparative studies of the continent's most linguistically complex region. Pacific Linguistics 552. Canberra. (whole volume; includes Harvey 'An initial reconstruction of Proto Gunwinyguan phonology' 205-268 and Alpher, Evans & Harvey 'Proto Gunwinyguan verb suffixes' 305-352)
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Full-text search of the 522-page volume: Uwinymil (Uw/U) appears only as a data language in sound-correspondence tables (/t/ reflex of *th, p. 212 region), cognate sets, verb-suffix tables ('occasional information from Uwinymil (U; Harvey field notes)') and pronominal forms. No stress statement for Uwinymil anywhere; stress passages concern Ngan'gityemerri, Warray, Dalabon, Gaagudju and general nonPN ('In nearly all nonPN languages, stress on disyllabic phonological words is on the first syllable', Harvey, Reconstruction of pronominals, p. 483).

sources.citation: Harvey, Mark. 2003. Western Gunwinyguan. In Nicholas Evans (ed.), The non-Pama-Nyungan languages of northern Australia, 285-303. Pacific Linguistics 552. Canberra.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Nothing on Uwinymil stress. p. 285: 'Uwinymil is poorly recorded, but the available materials suffice to establish that it was a distinct language (Harvey, to appear).' Uwinymil data used only for monosyllabic verb reduplication (pp. 289-293, Table 10) and the Aggrakundi=Uwinymil identification (p. 295). The one stress remark (p. 288, place names with stress on first and third syllables of four-syllable roots) concerns Warray, not Uwinymil. Reference list p. 302 cites 'Harvey, Mark, to appear, Uwinymil. In Blake & Dixon (eds) Handbook of Australian languages, vol. 6' - never published.

sources.citation: Schmidt, Wilhelm. 1917-1918 [publ. 1919]. Die Gliederung der australischen Sprachen (Fortsetzung). Anthropos 12-13: section 'D. Die Woolwoonga-Gruppe', pp. 441-443 (on Parkhouse's Aggrakundi and Awarra vocabularies).
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: No phonology beyond lexical comparison tables and the remark that Awarra may be a 'Mischsprache' diverging lexically from Aggrakundi; no Betonung/Akzent remark for this group.

sources.citation: Parkhouse, T. A. 1896 [read 6 Nov 1894]. Remarks on the native tongues in the neighbourhood of Port Darwin. Transactions of the Royal Society of South Australia 19: 1-18.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Wordlist source (the 'Aggrakundi' vocabulary, pp. 16-18, is Uwinymil per Harvey 2003:295). Orthography note (p. 7) covers vowel/consonant values and the aspirate only; no statement about accent or stress for any language. Some Aggrakundi items carry acute accents (kowonéro 'spear', méddoballi, dibbomélwon) but the key does not say whether these mark stress or vowel quality. Remarks on intonation/lengthening concern Wulnar and Larrakia.

sources.citation: Parkhouse, T. A. 1895. Native tribes of Port Darwin and its neighbourhood. Report of the Sixth Meeting of the Australasian Association for the Advancement of Science (Brisbane): 638-647.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Ethnographic; locates the Awinnmul and Aggrakundi between Fountain Head and Pine Creek and says their tongue is distinct from Awarra (Warray). No linguistic data on stress.
